additional_concerns: The PRESERVES findings below concern only the novel-or-complex exception, not the correctness of each complete relief model.

Candidates node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 convert preservation of existing application processing into a substantive exclusion from relief. The circular expressly preserves processing; whether that necessarily defeats relief, including after subsequent application decisions, remains unresolved. The procedural-preservation and relief-exclusion readings should remain distinct.

The relevant SFC FAQs and authoritative clarification of the transition are missing for resolving actual procedural availability. The supplied dependency IDs have null source hashes and no identifying descriptions, so neither can reliably be matched to those authorities. Applicable home-jurisdiction requirements and guidance on novel or complex features are also needed to resolve individual factual classifications.

The introductory immediate-effect wording and the express 28 November 2025 commencement provision require reconciliation for any disputed temporal application. The supplied text does not establish a universal proposed-implementation-date test. Candidate node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e also describes proposed implementation in its temporal basis while its formula tests assessment_date.

Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from scope, while node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa tests substantive conditions independently of application history. Neither answers actual relief availability for a pending legacy application; node.8eb374ffa546ddd2ba291e37 leaves that question unresolved and has no executable rule.

No candidate should infer an independent approval obligation, permission to bypass preserved processing, exemption from notification or post-vetting, or overall compliance from its Boolean result. The introductory reference to home supervision does not clearly establish an additional standalone item (ii) condition.
